profile.purpose: A walking tour of Asian Family Mart in North Seattle, Kenji's most-visited grocery store. He goes aisle by aisle, pointing out the produce, meats, seafood, pantry staples, frozen foods, drinks and kitchenware he buys there, with shopping tips along the way.
profile.thesis: Asian Family Mart is Kenji's favourite place to shop. He shows what it stocks that Western supermarkets don't, how its prices compare, and how he picks specific items there.
key_takeaways: Covers produce selection tips: wrinkly champagne mangoes, slightly giving mangosteens, and smooth-skinned ginger that doesn't need peeling.
Shows the store's range of mushrooms, eggplants, herbs, meats, offal, and live seafood such as Dungeness crab and spot prawns.
Explains the 'China Time-Honored Brand' label on traditional Chinese ingredients like doubanjiang and compares it to the French AOC and Italian DOP systems.
Introduces roasted rapeseed oil as the oil behind the signature flavour of much Sichuan cooking.
Names specific items he buys: Tamaki Gold rice, Arabiki sausages, the store's pork soup dumplings, pork steamed buns, Japanese curry blocks and Calpico.
Points to the store for cheap kitchenware: bowls, stacking stainless steel bowls, chopsticks, bamboo steamers, woks and papaya shredders.

outline.title: Introduction to Asian Mart
outline.summary: A cold-open teaser, then Kenji introduces Asian Family Mart in Seattle as his most-visited store for Asian ingredients and produce.

outline.title: Produce and fresh mushrooms
outline.summary: Covers fruit (champagne mangoes, durian, longans, mangosteens, dragon fruit, stone fruit) with tips for judging ripeness, then the cultivated mushroom selection and nagaimo for okonomiyaki.

outline.title: Greens, herbs, and roots
outline.summary: Greens and herbs such as Thai basil, mint, cilantro and dill, plus unusual fruits and a wide range of eggplant varieties. Also covers ginger selection, chilies, scallions, lemongrass and green papaya.

outline.title: Meats, sausages, and tofu
outline.summary: Miso, Japanese Arabiki sausages, packaged whole duck, Chinese sausages, dried seafood, tofu, dumpling wrappers, and fresh noodles that arrive on Mondays.

outline.title: Specialty butchery and offal
outline.summary: Shaved meats for hot pot and shabu shabu, pork parts, Snake River Farms and Mishima Reserve beef, short ribs for galbi, oxtail, and a large tripe and offal selection including beef aorta, tongue and pork jaw.

outline.title: Live seafood and dumplings
outline.summary: The live seafood tanks his son calls 'the small aquarium': oysters, spot prawns, cheap live Dungeness crab, and handmade frozen dumplings.

outline.title: Traditional pantry staples
outline.summary: Explains looking for the China Time-Honored Brand label on ingredients like doubanjiang, then tours the egg section (quail, duck, salted, tea, thousand-year), soy milk and Chinese cooking wines.

outline.title: Oils, rice, and snacks
outline.summary: Roasted rapeseed oil for Sichuan cooking, the rice selection including Tamaki Gold, Turtle Chips and the wide chip selection.

outline.title: Sauces, spices, and canned goods
outline.summary: Soy sauces from many countries, sugars, salt, MSG, dashi, chili crisp varieties, chili oils, curry pastes and blocks, fish pastes, and cheap spices like Sichuan pepper and chilies. Also covers a Sichuan YouTube chef's hot pot base, canned seafood and stinky tofu.

outline.title: Frozen buns and confectionery
outline.summary: Pork steamed buns for breakfast, candies and snacks like Hello Panda, Pocky and prawn crackers, and the frozen section's soup dumplings, shumai, crystal shrimp dumplings and banana leaves.

outline.title: Drinks and specialty items
outline.summary: The Asian drinks section and the story of why Calpis is sold as Calpico in the US.

outline.title: Noodles, tools, and wrap-up
outline.summary: The dry noodle aisle, then inexpensive bowls, bamboo steamers, woks, papaya shredders, chopsticks and stacking stainless steel bowls, before closing with the store's location.
